flags: Partial overview: both NCDOT cache files contain identical truncated guidebook text ending in the Flat Rock chapter, before Black Mountain Rag. Only the contents/index entry establishes inclusion; its specific designation rationale and naming history are unavailable.

Dropped unsupported current claims: fiddle-tune naming and road-playing metaphor, sharp curves and hairpins, seventeen-mile stretch, exact byway endpoints, designated Edneyville spur, and Black Mountains named for dark green firs. The album page does not substantiate the byway name.

The cache documents Helene damage and a June 2025 park reopening, but supplies no current road-manager conditions or full corridor reopening. Geographic sequence is not a current-access assurance; no fabricated driving advisory or dated practical note added.
No strip towns supplied; moment order follows the Bat Cave page’s explicit southeast sequence. Chimney Rock is a separate excursion because park features are not established as roadside views.
The original claim that the road passes below the monolith between Bat Cave and the village lacks support. Gneiss composition and the waterfall height are supported.
